newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T drops after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T drops after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc dropped in pre-market trading on Wednesday after the tobacco-to-insurance conglomerate posted a five percent rise in yearly pre-tax profits, no better than analysts had expected.
The stock, which has risen steadily through the past four months, was down 13p at 536-1/2 by 0810 GMT.
The company also doused hopes for a settlement of U.S. lawsuits on smoking-related diseases that have helped propel the stock in recent months.
It said the U.S. tobacco industry has no intention of proposing a settlement, though B.A.T added that it believed it had no liability from any claims because of its status as a holding company.

Traders pointed out that the headline pre-tax profit figure was below the consensus of expectations after B.A.T took a 160 million stg one-off charge due to U.S. environment claims at its insurance unit Eagle Star.
"We might see some fidgety selling today, the 160 million charge was a surprise but the figures were more or less in the middle of the range," said one trader.
"Basically the figures were a little bit less than expected because of the charge," said another, "but there is nothing really to worry about."
Pre-tax profit rose to 2.495 billion stg, compared with analyst expectations in a range between 2.586 million stg and 2.717 billion.

Chairman Lord Cairns said the company recognised that it had not acheved its objective of improving total shareholder returns in 1996 but still believed it could deliver superior total returns on a "sustainable basis."
